pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png with Read and it loaded as a 1024x1536 storyboard page with page number 3. It has five panels in three tiers: two at the top, two in the middle and one wide panel at the bottom. My natural reading order, left to right and top to bottom: (1) Top-left panel. Caption: 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' There are two face placeholders: raman on the left and slightly lower, meera on the right and higher. (2) Top-right panel. Caption: 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' One placeholder, priya, just under the caption. (3) Middle-left panel. Caption: 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' One placeholder, ravi, in the centre. (4) Middle-right panel. Caption: 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' No faces; the panel is empty below the caption. (5) Wide bottom panel. Caption at top-left: 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' A teal screen/sign box at top-right: 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12'. Three placeholders in a row near the bottom: raman, priya, ravi. There are no speech balloons on this page; all text is captions or the sign.
pages.observation: I did not misread the order. The three middle/top tiers split cleanly into left and right halves, the wide bottom panel comes last, and no caption or sign covers a face placeholder. Concrete issues: (a) 'A later morning' is a time jump, but on this image alone I cannot tell what it is later than. The art or the previous page needs to show the change of time or day clearly, or the caption is unanchored. (b) Panel 1 does not show who is the patient and who is staff. Raman and Meera are both just faces; the art must make Meera read as front-desk staff, if she is, and Raman as the patient checking in. Otherwise 'patients can always check in at the front desk' has no visible subject. (c) Panel 4 has no character, and its 'his' depends on carrying Ravi over from panel 3. That works only if the art clearly shows Ravi's hand or phone with the form. A blank background would leave 'his own phone' and 'shared with consent' unclear: shared with whom? (d) In panel 5, the order of the three placeholders (raman, priya, ravi) suggests a mapping to A-10/A-11/A-12, but nothing confirms it. Page 04 relies on Ravi being A-12, so the art or screen should tie Ravi to A-12 visibly, for example a name on the screen or a matching ticket. (e) Pacing: the page is all narrator captions with no dialogue or reaction, so it reads like a brochure explainer. Consider one line of speech or a visible reaction, such as Ravi glancing at the screen. (f) Panel 5 has a large empty area between the screen box and the figures. The art should put the screen where the characters can be seen looking at it, so the caption-to-screen link reads. Verdict: no reading-order failure, but (a), (c) and (d) are unresolved context/reference problems for the art and caption stage. I recommend changes-requested until they are addressed or justified.
